subject: Order form — phased billing & minimum commit breakdown
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitAI PO + request: phased billing vs. single min commit invoice

Ben / Aditya — forwarding OrbitAI's PO and the procurement note we got this morning. Key asks from Orbit: they want the minimum commit to be structured as a three‑phase schedule (Q2/Q3/Q4) rather than one upfront invoice, and they asked for net‑45 payment terms. Procurement also flagged VAT handling — they prefer Redwood to invoice without VAT and for Orbit to self‑account where required (they will provide the VAT reverse charge certificate if needed).

Questions for us before I reply to them:
- Can we accept a phased invoicing schedule for the minimum commit while keeping the order form language that ties credits to invoice milestones?
- Any constraints from finance on net‑45 vs our standard net‑30 for first‑year named accounts?
- Legal: is there risk with carrying over unused commit between phases (client wants a 90‑day carryover window) — Kimberly, can you comment on acceptable language?

Attached: OrbitAI_PO_20270420.pdf (procurement PO), their procurement email snippet inlined below.

Thanks — I want to propose a consolidated response by EOD so Ben can loop the customer in.

— Ava

[inline snippet from OrbitAI procurement: "We need the minimum commitment to be payable in three installments across the next three quarters. Our treasury requires net‑45. VAT will be handled on our side. Happy to provide supporting docs."]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@orbitai.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbitAI PO + request: phased billing vs. single min commit invoice

Rachel — thanks for sending this over and for the clarity on VAT. I copied our finance and legal leads so we can confirm the approach quickly. High level we can do a phased invoice plan for the minimum commit, subject to a few guardrails so both sides retain predictable economics. Proposed approach: 

1) Three invoices tied to quarter start dates: 2027‑07‑01 (Q3), 2027‑10‑01 (Q4), 2028‑01‑01 (Q1).
2) Each invoice equals one third of the committed seat/token value and is due net‑45 from the invoice date.
3) Unused credits from any phase can be carried forward for up to 90 days; after that, unused credits expire unless parties agree in writing.
4) If usage materially exceeds forecast (>125% of committed run‑rate) before the next scheduled invoice, we will consume overage at standard on‑demand rates and invoice monthly (no offset against future commit invoices).

Kimberly / Aditya — if this is acceptable I can send the amended order form via DocuSign for Orbit to sign and then route the first invoice on 2027‑07‑01. I'm attaching my suggested commercial redlines (redlines_orderform_v3.docx).

Rachel — can you confirm OrbitAI is OK with the three milestone dates above and the 90‑day carryover window? If you prefer specific calendar dates different from the proposed ones we can adjust.

Best,
Ben

Attachments: redlines_orderform_v3.docx (commercial redlines, tracked)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbitAI PO + request: phased billing vs. single min commit invoice

Ava / Ben — quick legal wash on the proposed commercial structure. A few redline items I recommend before we send to the customer: 

- Invoice timing: tie invoice issuance to "Milestone Date" language in the Order Form rather than a calendar date to avoid ambiguity if the effective date shifts.
- Refund / credit expiry: 90‑day carryover is OK but add an explicit exception for material non‑payment by Redwood (e.g., if we owe credits due to systemic downtime) — client should be able to apply credits within one year in that exceptional case.
- Net terms: net‑45 is fine for this customer provided we keep the payment security clause — request a customer PO number and an initial deposit (first milestone invoice charged on or immediately after DocuSign completion) if legal holds for net‑45 require additional mitigation.
- Taxes: include clause "Customer is responsible for VAT, GST, and other consumption taxes; Redwood will itemize taxes on invoices where Redwood is required to collect". If Orbit provides VAT registration / reverse charge docs, we will zero‑rate VAT as appropriate.
- Audit right: tighten audit language to limit customer audit to once per 12 months and scope to billing records for the prior 12 months to avoid broad legal exposure.

I tracked these in redlines_orderform_v3.docx but summarized here so Ben can speak to them with Orbit.

Kimberly
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@orbitai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@orbitai.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitAI PO + request: phased billing vs. single min commit invoice

Ben / Ava — thanks for the quick turnaround. The three milestone dates look workable. Two items from procurement/treasury: 

1) We will confirm the VAT reverse‑charge docs by next week and send the PO number for the first milestone.
2) Orbit requests the first invoice be issued on DocuSign completion (we expect to sign within 5 business days after you send). For cashflow reasons we prefer the first invoice to be payable net‑45 from invoice date as you proposed.

On the carryover: 90 days is acceptable; procurement asked if we can extend the carryover to 120 days in case of variable consumption between teams. Are you open to giving a single exception to 120 days if we can jointly agree on a usage forecast? Not a blocker, just a request.

If you can send updated order form via DocuSign with the redlines incorporated we will sign and route PO.

— Rachel
Purchasing Lead, OrbitAI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OrbitAI PO + request: phased billing vs. single min commit invoice — finance confirms path

Team — quick finance confirmation after reviewing the PO and Kimberly's redlines: 

- Net‑45: approved for OrbitAI on this agreement; require invoice reference to the OrbitAI PO number and tracking in our AR system (we'll request the PO in the DocuSign request).
- Phased invoicing: approved on the condition that the first milestone invoice is paid on or before 2027‑08‑15 (net‑45 from an expected 2027‑07‑01 invoice date) and that the order form includes the "Milestone Date" linkage Kimberly suggested. If the first invoice misses payment by >30 days we reserve the right to suspend access to dedicated capacity under the Reserved Capacity Addendum until payment is cured.
- VAT: finance will zero‑rate invoices if Orbit provides valid reverse‑charge documentation; otherwise taxes will be billed per standard procedure.
- Action: Ben, please prepare the DocuSign package with attached redlines and include a required PO number field. Also add a short billing FAQ (1‑page) for procurement to reduce back‑and‑forth on invoice expectations.

I'll validate the final invoice metadata before each milestone is published.

Thanks — Aditya
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
